findings.title: Validation has a write side effect that inflates match counts on every validation run
findings.body: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, which increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and saves the row. Validation is supposed to be a read-only check, but every call to `valid?`, including repeated calls from `save` retries, controller paths, or `DiscourseHub` registration (`user.valid?` is called in `UsersController#create` before `save`), counts as a new block. The statistics become inaccurate, and each validation issues an extra UPDATE. The increment belongs in a separate, explicit step after the user is actually rejected.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses increments
findings.body: `should_block?` loads the record, does `record.match_count += 1`, and then calls `record.save`. Concurrent signups with the same blocked address race on this, so some increments are lost. `last_match_at` is also overwritten by whichever save lands last. Using an atomic `update_counters` / `UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1` avoids the lost update. The `record.save` also runs model validations (including the uniqueness query) on every match, which is unnecessary for a counter update.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive while user emails are downcased
findings.body: `should_block?` does `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` with the raw value, and the uniqueness check on `BlockedEmail` is also case-sensitive. The app normalises user emails with `Email.downcase` in several places (for example `change_email` and `find_by_username_or_email`). An entry such as `bad@spam.com` is therefore not matched against `Bad@Spam.com`, so a blocked address can register by changing letter case. The lookup and stored value should be normalised consistently.

findings.title: Returning the full errors hash and submitted values is a new response contract
findings.body: The failure response now includes `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values` with name, username, and email. The JavaScript client uses `result.errors.email` and `result.values.email` to add the address to `rejectedEmails`. Any validation error on the email attribute, including format errors and 'already taken', now causes the value to be blacklisted client-side until the user edits it. This couples the UI to server error keys and changes the API shape for every caller of `/users`, with no tests covering the new fields.

findings.title: Rejected email is recorded for any email-field error, not only the blocked case
findings.body: `createAccount` pushes `result.values.email` into `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` exists. That includes ordinary errors such as an invalid format or an address already in use, where the user should see the specific reason. The client then shows the generic `user.email.invalid` reason for the rejected value, which hides the server's message. The list also grows without bound during a session and is never cleared.

findings.title: Validator spec does not cover the side effect or the whitelist/blacklist interaction
findings.body: The spec stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, so the real counting and saving behaviour is never exercised through the validator. There is no test that validating twice does not double-count, and no test that a record already failing the domain whitelist/blacklist skips the blocked check, which the `record.errors[attribute].blank?` guard implies. The new `user.email.blocked` message is also not asserted.

findings.title: Concurrency and case handling are untested
findings.body: The model spec covers the single-threaded happy path only. It does not test that matching is case-insensitive (see `should_block?`), and it does not test concurrent increments of `match_count`. The `be_within_one_second_of` matcher and the `Timecop` dependency are also used without a visible dependency in this change.

findings.title: PR description is a placeholder
findings.body: The description reads only 'Test 3', so the PR gives no explanation of the new blocklist behaviour, the response contract change in `UsersController#create`, or the removal of the email validator from `User` in favour of the new `EmailValidator`. Maintainers cannot review intent from it.
